title: Enema
what: Water or a solution is put into the rectum to clean out the bowel. It is simple and usually does not hurt.
why: For constipation, before bowel tests and surgery, and sometimes before childbirth if needed.
duration: usually 10 to 20 minutes, including emptying your bowel
tell_doctor: Hemorrhoids, fissures, or pain in the anus

prepare.title: Toilet
prepare.text: Find out where the nearest toilet is. The urge may come quickly.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear clothes that are easy to take off below the waist. You can bring spare underwear.

steps: You lie on your left side and pull your knees up to your belly
The nurse lubricates the tip and gently puts it into the anus
The solution flows in slowly. Breathe through your mouth, deeply and calmly
Lie still and hold it for as long as the nurse says, usually 5 to 10 minutes
Then you go to the toilet
feel: A feeling of fullness and an urge to go to the toilet
Sometimes belly cramps. Breathe deeper and tell the nurse
after: After emptying your bowel, you can go back to your day
If the enema is before a test, follow your clinic's instructions
red_flags: Bleeding from the anus, strong belly pain, dizziness, or weakness: see a doctor right away or call emergency services

faq.a: Usually not. The fullness and the urge to go can be unpleasant. If it hurts, tell the nurse.

faq.q: How long should I hold it after an enema?
faq.a: Usually 5 to 10 minutes. The nurse will tell you exactly. This helps the solution soften the stool.
